subject: astronomy
title: Big Bang: Expansion and Hubble's Law
welcome_lead: Galaxies fly apart because space itself is stretching.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: redshift, Hubble's law and an expanding universe.
final_note: Hubble's law is the first hard evidence for a Big Bang origin.

concepts.def: Stretching of light wavelengths from receding sources.
v = H0 d — recession speed scales with distance.
On large scales the universe is homogeneous and isotropic.
The hot, dense early state from which the universe expanded.

walkthroughs.body_html: Light from receding galaxies is redshifted — wavelengths grow longer as space expands. Edwin Hubble showed in 1929 that more distant galaxies recede faster, leading to Hubble's law.
v = H0 d: recession speed equals the Hubble constant times distance. With H0 around 70 km/s/Mpc, a galaxy 100 Mpc away recedes at about 7000 km/s.
The universe is assumed homogeneous (same density everywhere) and isotropic (same in every direction) on the largest scales. There is no privileged centre to the expansion.
